name: office
title: A small office server
summary: One server that receives an office's mail from the Internet, holds its mailboxes and sends what its people write. Spam filtering, greylisting and the auto-ban are on at the shipped thresholds, spam a domain asks to hold is held in the quarantine, passwords are held to a policy and checked against known breaches, a signed-in person sends only as themselves, and a browser session lasts a working day.
steps: Give the submission port (587) STARTTLS with a certificate, or add port 465 with TLS: a port's security is the port's, not a setting, and the checklist's submission item says which port still takes a password in the clear.
Switch each domain's quarantine digest and external-sender tag on in the domain's own settings: both are a domain's choice, and the server has no value of them to set.
Set quarantine_digest_base_url to the address the webmail answers on, or the digest has no links to send.

entries.name: usespf
entries.why: a forged sender is the commonest spam, and SPF is the cheapest test of it

entries.name: usemxchecks
entries.why: a sender domain that cannot receive mail cannot be answered, so its mail is scored

entries.name: ASDKIMVerificationEnabled
entries.why: a verified signature is what DMARC, the reports and the brand logos build on

entries.name: ASDMARCEnabled
entries.why: the sender domain's own policy says what to do with a forgery of it

entries.name: spammarkthreshold
entries.why: the shipped score at which a message is spam, written down so the diff shows it

entries.name: spamdeletethreshold
entries.why: the shipped score at which a message is refused, well clear of the mark

entries.name: antispamaddheaderspam
entries.why: a mail client's own junk filter can act on the X-hMailServer-Spam header

entries.name: antispamprependsubject
entries.why: people see at a glance that a message was judged spam

entries.name: usegreylisting
entries.why: most spam software does not retry, and a real server retries within the hour

entries.name: BypassGreylistingOnSPFSuccess
entries.why: a sender whose SPF passes is not delayed by greylisting

entries.name: BypassGreylistingOnMailFromMX
entries.why: mail from the sender domain's own MX host is not delayed either

entries.name: QuarantineEnabled
entries.why: spam a domain asks to hold is kept for people to release rather than delivered or lost

entries.name: AuthenticationResultsEnabled
entries.why: the server's verdicts are written into each message, where a mail client and the brand logos read them

entries.name: AutoBanOnLogonFailureEnabled
entries.why: an address that guesses passwords is shut out

entries.name: MaxInvalidLogonAttempts
entries.why: five failures before a ban, so that one mistyped password is not one

entries.name: LogonAttemptsWithinMinutes
entries.why: the shipped window the failures are counted in

entries.name: AutoBanMinutes
entries.why: an hour's ban stops a guessing run and lets a person back in after lunch

entries.name: AccountLockoutThreshold
entries.why: an account guessed at from many addresses is locked for a while as well

entries.name: authallowplaintext
entries.why: a password is never taken over a connection without TLS

entries.name: SmtpAuthenticatedSenderCheck
entries.why: a signed-in person sends as their own address, an alias of it, or a mailbox that granted them Send-As

entries.name: MaxSubmissionsPerIPPerMinute
entries.why: a stolen password cannot pour a thousand messages a minute through one address

entries.name: PasswordPolicyMinimumLength
entries.why: a short password is the one guessed first

entries.name: PasswordPolicyRejectCommon
entries.why: the passwords every guessing list starts with are refused

entries.name: BreachCheckEnabled
entries.why: a password already in a published breach is refused, and only five characters of its SHA-1 leave the server

entries.name: disconnectinvalidclients
entries.why: a client that sends nonsense is disconnected rather than answered for ever

entries.name: maximumincorrectcommands
entries.why: twenty wrong commands is a probe, not a confused mail client

entries.name: maxmessagesize
entries.why: 25 MB, what most providers accept, so a message sent here can be sent on

entries.name: SessionIdleSeconds
entries.why: a webmail or Deck session left open on a desk ends after half an hour unused

entries.name: SessionLifetimeSeconds
entries.why: no browser session outlives a ten-hour working day

entries.name: CreateDefaultSpecialUseFolders
entries.why: a new account has Drafts, Sent, Junk and Trash before its first client connects

entries.name: enableattachmentblocking
entries.why: an attachment on the blocked list, such as a program, is taken off before anybody opens it

entries.name: RecoverDeletedDays
entries.why: a message somebody deleted by mistake can be put back for two weeks

entries.name: ReputationWatchEnabled
entries.why: the server says when its own address appears on a block list
